mfg1-mechanical-source-guide-5s4s.title: Check the difference between 5S and 4S through ongoing activities
mfg1-mechanical-source-guide-5s4s.objective: Distinguish the five elements of 5S and the element omitted in 4S. Connect the names to daily actions.

paragraphs.title: Maintain the five elements
paragraphs.text: 5S consists of sorting, setting in order, cleaning, maintaining cleanliness, and discipline. Sorting removes unnecessary items; setting in order puts necessary items in designated places; cleaning removes dirt while also noticing small abnormalities such as oil leaks. Maintaining cleanliness means preserving the good condition achieved by sorting, setting in order, and cleaning. Discipline means making the rules agreed by everyone into habits.

paragraphs.title: Do not confuse what 4S omits
paragraphs.text: The material gives an example that calls sorting, setting in order, cleaning, and maintaining cleanliness “4S,” omitting discipline from 5S. Replacing cleaning with responsibility to make 5S, or adding responsibility to 4S, does not explain these names. Learn the names and also check which actions should be continued.

paragraphs.title: Do not stop after one attempt
paragraphs.text: 5S is not finished after tidying up once. Continue it every day to support a safe, comfortable workplace and good products. Do not discard documents or items entrusted to you on your own authority. If you find an abnormality, inform the responsible person from a safe situation. Do not put your hands into rotating parts to clean them.

terms.meaning: A name combining sorting, setting in order, cleaning, and maintaining cleanliness.
Continuing rather than doing something only once.

mfg1-mechanical-source-guide-5s4s.activity:
4 minutes: Write the elements of 5S and 4S separately.
5 minutes: Read the text and explain the difference between cleaning and maintaining cleanliness.
4 minutes: Imagine a workplace and write two daily actions and two people responsible for checking them.
2 minutes: Reflect on why responsibility must not replace cleaning.
safety: Study on paper. Follow workplace authority limits and safety procedures for cleaning, disposal, and approaching equipment.
mfg1-mechanical-source-guide-5s4s.summary: Do not replace cleaning in 5S with responsibility. 4S is a name that omits discipline; maintain a good condition every day.

mfg1-surface-source-guide-exam-study.title: Check the surface-treatment examination guide and how to study
mfg1-surface-source-guide-exam-study.objective: Distinguish the examination format, examples of work, and examination precautions stated in the material from the app’s practice scoring.

paragraphs.title: The material’s reference date and examination format
paragraphs.text: The outline in the material is current as of July (7) 2026. It explains that the examination checks skills requiring a considerable level of knowledge or experience, at a level equivalent to Grade 3 of the trade skills test, enabling a person to immediately carry out work to a certain level without special development or training. It describes a CBT format, 30 true-or-false theory questions, and 10 multiple-choice practical questions assessing judgment, planning, and related abilities. Theory and practical sections each last 40 minutes, and Japanese kanji have furigana readings. The name “practical” does not mean operating actual equipment in this format.

paragraphs.title: Separate passing standards from eligibility
paragraphs.text: The material gives passing standards of at least 65% for theory and at least 60% for practical. When this app’s independently created questions are scored with equal points per question, at least 20/30 in theory and 6/10 in practical are required independently; a combined score cannot compensate for either section. This does not guarantee the official, undisclosed point allocation. In principle, the material specifies foreign nationals who are at least 17 years old on the examination day, or at least 18 for Indonesian nationals, and who intend to work in Japan after passing. Check the organizer’s latest guidance on applications, eligibility, permitted items, and other matters. Do not decide eligibility for the current examination solely from the ages written in this material.

paragraphs.title: Category and examples of work
paragraphs.text: The material lists electroplating, hot-dip galvanizing, anodizing, and buff polishing as examples corresponding to the metal surface-treatment category. Examples of work and the scope of work you are authorized to perform are separate matters. Check the training, qualifications, and work authorization for each piece of equipment at your assigned workplace.

paragraphs.title: Protect examination fairness
paragraphs.text: The material prohibits taking actual questions or answers out of the examination, including partial information, and sharing them through social media or similar channels, whether publicly or privately. It describes this as serious misconduct that undermines fairness among examinees. It states that venues have surveillance cameras and proctors who monitor behavior during the examination. Misconduct may result in severe measures, including invalidation of results, loss of future examination eligibility, and notification to the Immigration Services Agency of Japan. Follow the organizer’s rules for details. The app’s questions are independently created and do not reproduce official questions.

paragraphs.title: Study Japanese and technical vocabulary
paragraphs.text: If the Japanese text is difficult, also continue studying Japanese. Ask supervisors, colleagues, or others specific questions about unfamiliar technical terms. Understand the meaning and read repeatedly, checking the sentence through to its end, including its subject, conditions, and negation. Do not practice using only the combined total of 80 minutes; manage the two 40-minute sections separately.

terms.meaning: A question that asks whether a statement is correct or incorrect.
Examples of jobs corresponding to a category.
The end of a sentence, which is also important for understanding negation and conditions.

mfg1-surface-source-guide-exam-study.activity:
4 minutes: Write the format, time, and standard for theory and practical in separate columns.
5 minutes: Distinguish the material’s reference date and stated ages from checking the latest guidance.
4 minutes: Organize the four examples of work and compare independently written affirmative and negative sentences.
2 minutes: Check ways to study without taking official questions out of the examination.
safety: Do not confuse passing a mock test with eligibility to work or authorization to perform workplace tasks. Do not collect, reproduce, or share actual examination questions or answers.
mfg1-surface-source-guide-exam-study.summary: Distinguish the material’s reference date from the latest guidance. Check the two examination requirements, four examples of work, fair handling of information, and reading through sentence endings.

mfg1-surface-source-guide-basic-safety.title: Check basic work safety and tool handling
mfg1-surface-source-guide-basic-safety.objective: Connect the explanation of occupational accidents with actions concerning rules, unfamiliar equipment, tools, and reporting abnormalities.

paragraphs.title: Accidents during work and commuting
paragraphs.text: Manufacturing workplaces have hazards such as high temperatures, heavy objects, machines, and chemicals. The material explains occupational accidents as injuries or illnesses caused by work or commuting. Everyone should work on prevention and follow workplace rules to protect both themselves and people around them. Do not determine the legal recognition of an individual case from this lesson alone.

paragraphs.title: Unfamiliar tools and tools after use
paragraphs.text: Do not touch unfamiliar machines or tools without authorization; check with your supervisor. Handle tools carefully, do not throw them to another person or leave them carelessly, and return them to the correct place after use. Feeling that there is no visible danger does not justify bypassing laws or rules.

paragraphs.title: Stop and report abnormalities
paragraphs.text: If you notice unusual sounds, smells, vibrations, or similar signs, stop the equipment safely using its specified procedure, report the facts and your response to your supervisor, and obtain instructions. Do not assume the inside is safe merely because the equipment has stopped. Also check your authority to restart it or inspect the inside.

terms.meaning: In the material, injuries or illnesses caused by work or commuting.
Handling something attentively rather than roughly.
Informing the responsible person of facts that differ from normal conditions and the actions taken.

mfg1-surface-source-guide-basic-safety.activity:
4 minutes: Organize imaginary cases during work and commuting.
5 minutes: Write the actions for passing tools to another person and returning them.
4 minutes: Prepare a request for advice for two situations: an unfamiliar machine and an unusual sound.
2 minutes: Reflect on rules that protect you and those around you.
safety: Do not run unfamiliar equipment as an experiment. Do not throw tools. Follow equipment procedures and authority limits for stopping, inspecting, and restarting.
mfg1-surface-source-guide-basic-safety.summary: Prevent accidents for your own sake and for those around you. Handle tools carefully and do not proceed on your own judgment when something is unfamiliar or abnormal.

mfg1-surface-source-guide-ph.title: Use pH 7 as the reference to distinguish acidity and alkalinity
mfg1-surface-source-guide-ph.objective: Distinguish the region near neutrality from the acidic and alkaline sides in introductory examples, and record the liquid’s identification and temperature.

paragraphs.title: Reading introductory examples
paragraphs.text: The material describes pH as an indicator of the degree of acidity or alkalinity of an aqueous solution. On an introductory scale of 0–14, it identifies pH 7 as neutral, values below 7 as acidic, and values above 7 as alkaline. Under the same introductory conditions, smaller values indicate stronger acidity and larger values stronger alkalinity.

paragraphs.title: Do not omit conditions
paragraphs.text: Comparing neutrality with approximately 7 is an introductory example for dilute aqueous solutions at room temperature. Do not omit temperature or liquid conditions and generalize that every liquid must fall within 0–14. Associate measurements with the liquid’s identification, temperature, method, and date and time. Do not decide that a liquid of unknown composition is harmless water merely because its value is near neutral.

terms.meaning: The condition used as a reference for comparing acidity and alkalinity in introductory examples.
In introductory examples, the side below neutral pH 7.
In introductory examples, the side above neutral pH 7.

mfg1-surface-source-guide-ph.activity:
4 minutes: Classify pH 3, 7, and 10 as acidic, neutral, or alkaline in an introductory example.
5 minutes: Read why comparing values differs from judging a liquid’s safety.
4 minutes: Create an imaginary record form including identification, temperature, method, and date and time.
2 minutes: Confirm that 0–14 must not be generalized to all liquids.
safety: Study only on paper. Do not mix acids and alkalis or identify unknown liquids by smell, taste, or contact with bare hands.
mfg1-surface-source-guide-ph.summary: In introductory examples, values below 7 are acidic and those above are alkaline. Keep values together with their conditions; pH alone does not guarantee safety.

mfg1-surface-source-guide-specific-gravi.title: Read specific-gravity examples using water at 4°C as the reference
mfg1-surface-source-guide-specific-gravi.objective: Check the specific-gravity reference and the material’s own example values without confusing them with density units or values in another table.

paragraphs.title: Reference and units
paragraphs.text: For the specific gravity of solids and liquids, the material uses water at 4°C as the reference and gives the reference specific gravity as 1. Specific gravity is a ratio to the reference density; do not attach density units such as g/cm³ directly to it. For equal volumes, it can also be considered as the mass ratio of the sample to the reference, but it is not calculated by directly dividing two masses of different volumes.

paragraphs.title: Six example values in the material
paragraphs.text: The examples on printed page 39 are aluminum 2.68, iron 7.87, nickel 8.69, copper 8.82, lead 11.43, and gold 19.32. These are reference values stated at this location; do not replace them without authorization with values from the later table of 21 metals or another source. Alloys and conditions can produce differences, so these values do not guarantee certified values for actual materials or exact values that remain unchanged at every temperature. In practice, follow the specified material specifications, reference, temperature, and verification method.

terms.meaning: The ratio to the density of a reference substance.
The substance used as the basis for comparison.
An example value checked together with its source and conditions.

mfg1-surface-source-guide-specific-gravi.activity:
4 minutes: Write the relationship between water at 4°C, specific gravity 1, and a ratio without units.
5 minutes: Check the six example values paired with their material names.
4 minutes: On paper, calculate the ratio of a 60 g sample to a 20 g reference of equal volume, and create fields for recording the source and temperature.
2 minutes: Reflect on why values must not be overwritten without authorization using another table.
safety: Do not judge an unidentified material or liquid to be safe or to meet the specified material requirement, and then use it, based on specific gravity alone.
mfg1-surface-source-guide-specific-gravi.summary: In the material, water at 4°C is the reference with specific gravity 1. Preserve the sources of the six example values; they do not replace checking actual material specifications.
